While investigating something related to the Waterproof Genre, I ran into the following:

https://github.com/leanprover/verso/blob/main/src/verso-manual/VersoManual/InlineLean.lean#L154 is not actually reached by the code right now, since config.error is a Boolean.

For Waterproof, we can't say a priori if a block will or will not have errors, since students can often edit them, so having none is the right setting for us. I have a commit patching this here: https://github.com/pimotte/verso/commit/cca50154b367dc7bbcd30e49e99c1abd9980e3f5

Hmm, I think we should ensure that we can keep the convenient flag syntax even if the flag is optional, rather than requiring the more verbose named-argument syntax. That's doable.

I would think that for your case, a custom block would make more sense than patching the built-in one. The one you linked to is really intended for authors. But perhaps it's soon time for a quick demo, just so I can see how you're using the various features?
(where "demo" could also be "please check out this revision of these three repos and click in these ways, noticing these aspects" if you wanted)

David Thrane Christiansen said:

Hmm, I think we should ensure that we can keep the convenient flag syntax even if the flag is optional, rather than requiring the more verbose named-argument syntax. That's doable.

I would think that for your case, a custom block would make more sense than patching the built-in one. The one you linked to is really intended for authors. But perhaps it's soon time for a quick demo, just so I can see how you're using the various features?

Side note for the flag: Do note that with the commit above the default behaviour changes to "don't expect anything", rather than "expect no errors", which might also be counterproductive for the manual.

With respect to custom block, I had also been thinking about that, I think it might be where we want to end up.

I think doing a demo makes sense soonish, I think we're pretty close to figuring out what we want on our side. I'll come back to you for this:)

For the root cause of the issue I just ran into, I think it's kind of ambiguous if https://github.com/leanprover/verso/blob/ba73c2308107d93208d08ca20b08a0c7c1c8a900/src/verso-manual/VersoManual/InlineLean.lean#L157 matches the description of that function. (For our usecase, not silencing the messages in the default case is what we want), but I'm not sure if this is what you'd want for the Manual Genre, which strengthens the idea we should just implement our own block.
Yeah, sounds like that. Please do suggest opportunities for making it easier for you to do so, if there's any refactoring of the InlineLean module that exposes helpers you find useful for this.
